original_interpretation: Synopsys' FY2025 revenue was 62.0% EDA, 24.8% design IP, 10.7% Ansys (simulation, acquired) and 2.5% other.
evidence_found: "The following table shows the percentage of revenue by product groups" ... Year Ended October 31, 2025: "EDA | 62.0 %", "Design IP | 24.8 %", "Ansys | 10.7 %", "Other | 2.5 %", "Total | 100.0 %" (10-K FY2025, Revenue note, Disaggregated Revenue table)
notes: FY ends 31 Oct 2025; Ansys share reflects partial-year consolidation after the acquisition. Prior year design IP was 31.1%.

original_interpretation: Synopsys had about US$11.4 billion of contracted backlog at 31 October 2025, including US$2.0 billion of non-cancellable Flexible Spending Account commitments where customers choose products later.
evidence_found: "Contracted but unsatisfied or partially unsatisfied performance obligations (backlog) were approximately $11.4 billion as of October 31, 2025, which includes $2.0 billion in non-cancellable Flexible Spending Account (FSA) commitments from customers where actual product selection and quantities ... are to be determined by customers at a later date." (10-K FY2025, Revenue note)
notes: Excludes future sales-based royalties, as the metric population says.

original_interpretation: Synopsys recognised US$125.3 million of sales-based royalties in FY2025 (US$104.4 million in FY2024), a small part of a model dominated by licences.
evidence_found: "During fiscal 2025 and 2024, we recognized $125.3 million and $104.4 million, respectively, from performance obligations satisfied from sales-based royalties earned during the periods." (10-K FY2025, Revenue note)
correction: The figures are verified. The source does not say the model is 'dominated by licences'; that clause is the researcher's reading and needs the total-revenue/licence split from elsewhere in the 10-K.
notes: The cited R14 page gives no total revenue or licence-revenue line, so 'a small part' cannot be checked from this page.

original_interpretation: Rambus mixes three revenue types: memory-interface chip sales (direct and via distributors), patent and technology licence royalties, and contract/other revenue (software licences, engineering fees, support).
evidence_found: "The Company’s revenue consists of product, royalties and contract and other revenue. Products primarily consist of memory interface chips sold directly and indirectly to module manufacturers and OEMs worldwide through multiple channels, including its direct sales force and distributors. Royalties revenue consists of patent and technology license royalties. Contract and other revenue consists of software license fees, engineering fees ... and support and maintenance fees." (10-K FY2025, Summary of Significant Accounting Policies)

original_interpretation: Rambus patent and technology licences generally run one to ten years and pay fixed amounts over time, guaranteed minimums, variable royalties based on the licensee's sales or use, or a mix.
evidence_found: "Rambus’ patent and technology licensing arrangements generally range between one year and ten years in duration" ... "result in fixed payments received over time, with guaranteed minimum payments on occasion, variable payments calculated based on the licensee’s sale or use of the IP, or a mix of fixed and variable payments." (10-K FY2025, Royalties Revenue)

original_interpretation: For fixed-fee licences Rambus recognises revenue when the IP right transfers, net of a financing component computed at customer-specific rates typically of 5% to 10%.
evidence_found: "For fixed-fee arrangements (including arrangements that include minimum guaranteed amounts), the Company recognizes revenue upon control over the underlying IP use right transferring to the licensee, net of the effect of significant financing components calculated using customer-specific, risk-adjusted lending rates typically ranging between 5% and 10%" (10-K FY2025, Royalties Revenue)
notes: Interest income on the financing component is recognised over time on an effective-rate basis.

original_interpretation: Ceva, a pure IP licensor, earned US$63.6 million licence revenue and US$46.0 million royalty revenue in 2025 (total US$109.6 million).
evidence_found: Note 2 Disaggregation (Details), $ in thousands, Dec. 31 2025: "Revenues | $ 109,598"; "License [Member] | Revenues | 63,595"; "Royalty [Member] | Revenues | 46,003" (Royalty all "Transferred at Point in Time") (10-K FY2025, R56)
notes: 'Other' revenue was 0 in 2025, consistent with an all-licence/royalty model; the 'pure IP licensor' label itself is not stated on this XBRL page.

original_interpretation: Photronics contracts to sell sets of photomasks (one mask per layer), invoices most layers as they ship, and recognises revenue over time because custom masks have no alternative use and it has a right to payment for work done.
evidence_found: "The Company typically contracts with the Company’s customers to sell sets of photomasks, which are comprised of multiple layers, the predominance of which the Company invoices as they ship to customers. As the photomasks are manufactured to customer specifications, they have no alternative use ... right to payment for work completed to date, the Company recognizes revenue ... “over time,” on most of the Company’s contracts." (10-K FY2025, Note 1)
notes: 'One mask per layer' is a gloss; the source says sets 'comprised of multiple layers'.

original_interpretation: Photronics' photomasks have no list prices: each transaction price is individually negotiated, and the vast majority of contracts carry only fixed consideration.
evidence_found: "their transaction prices are individually established through negotiations with customers; consequently, the Company’s photomasks do not have standard or “list” prices. The transaction prices of the vast majority of the Company’s revenue contracts include only fixed amounts of consideration." (10-K FY2025, Note 1, Revenue Recognition)

original_interpretation: Photronics' order backlog is generally no more than one to two weeks for IC photomasks, so a merchant mask maker has almost no forward revenue visibility.
evidence_found: "the Company’s backlog of orders is generally not in excess of one to two weeks for IC photomasks and two to three weeks for FPD photomasks." (10-K FY2025, Note 1, Remaining Performance Obligations)
correction: The backlog figure is verified for Photronics. 'So a merchant mask maker has almost no forward revenue visibility' is the researcher's inference, generalised from one company; it is not stated in the filing.

original_interpretation: Amkor recognises packaging and test revenue over time as services are rendered (generally over two to three weeks), using a cost-plus-margin input method, because its services create or enhance the customer's wafer.
evidence_found: "We recognize revenue as services are rendered, which generally occurs over the course of two to three weeks." ... "We recognize revenue over time as services are rendered because our services create or enhance the customer’s wafer. We utilize an input method (cost incurred plus estimated margin)" (10-K FY2025, Note 1)

original_interpretation: Amkor's packaging and test prices are negotiated per customer to reflect the customised nature of each service (customer-specific stand-alone selling prices), and services are generally billed at completion of each packaging or test step.
evidence_found: "our negotiated pricing reflects the customized nature of our services and represents a customer-specific stand-alone selling price." ... "Services are generally billed at completion of each individual packaging or test service or in some instances at the completion of all services in a combined offering." (10-K FY2025, Note 1)

original_interpretation: Amkor's contract liabilities from customer advance payments rose to US$390.8 million at end-2025 from US$95.6 million at end-2024, with US$100 million of standby letters of credit outstanding against advances.
evidence_found: "Contract liabilities were $390.8 million and $95.6 million as of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, respectively. The increase in contract liabilities was primarily due to higher customer advance payments in 2025." ... "As of December 31, 2025, $100.0 million of standby letters of credit were issued and outstanding related to customer advance payments received." (10-K FY2025, Note 1)
notes: Short-term portion was $69.6m at end-2025.

original_interpretation: Applied Materials recognises equipment and spare-parts revenue at a point in time on shipment or delivery, and service-agreement revenue over time, typically within 12 months.
evidence_found: "We recognize revenue from equipment and spares parts at a point in time when we have satisfied our performance obligation by transferring control of the goods to the customer, which typically occurs at shipment or delivery. Revenue from service agreements is recognized over time, typically within 12 months" (10-K FY2025, Note 1)

original_interpretation: Applied Materials collects most of the price within a set number of days of shipment, with the remainder typically due on customer technical acceptance; it may also take customer deposits.
evidence_found: "Generally, the majority of payments are due within a certain number of days from shipment of goods or performance of service. The remainder is typically due upon customer technical acceptance. In certain circumstances we may receive deposits from customers for future deliverables." (10-K FY2025, Note 1, Payment Terms)

original_interpretation: Applied Materials treats a service agreement as one performance obligation that can bundle multiple goods and services delivered against a performance metric.
evidence_found: "Our service agreements are considered one performance obligation and may include multiple goods and services that we provide to the customer to deliver against a performance metric." (10-K FY2025, Note 1)

original_interpretation: KLA sells perpetual and term software licences, recognises licence revenue at a point in time when the software is made available, and recognises bundled post-contract support ratably.
evidence_found: "We offer perpetual and term licenses for software products." ... "Revenue from software licenses is recognized at a point in time, when the software is made available to the customer. Revenue from PCS is deferred at contract inception and recognized ratably over the service period, or as services are performed." (10-K FY2026, Note 1)

original_interpretation: KLA's equipment payment terms generally require 70-90% of contract value within 30-60 days of shipment, with the remainder due within 30 days of acceptance.
evidence_found: "Our payment terms and conditions vary by contract type, although terms generally include a requirement of payment of 70% to 90% of total contract consideration within 30 to 60 days of shipment, with the remainder payable within 30 days of acceptance." (10-K FY2026, Revenue note R11)

original_interpretation: KLA's FY2026 revenue of US$13.58 billion was US$10.45 billion product and US$3.13 billion service (about 23% service).
evidence_found: Consolidated Statements of Operations, $ thousands, 12 months ended Jun. 30, 2026: "Total revenues | $ 13,579,476"; Product "Total revenues | $ 10,453,537"; Service "Total revenues | $ 3,125,939" (10-K FY2026, R5)
notes: Checker computed service share 3,125,939/13,579,476 = 23.0%.

original_interpretation: ASML generally obtains a right to payment for systems through reservation of a production slot and/or on delivery, with the rest on final acceptance; payment is typically due 15-45 days after those events and contracts typically include cancellation penalties.
evidence_found: "we generally obtain a right to payment for our systems through a reservation of a production slot and/or upon delivery of our systems, with the remaining portion upon final acceptance of our systems." ... "The payment is typically due 15–45 days after the aforementioned events. Our contracts typically include cancellation penalties" (20-F FY2025, Revenue note)

original_interpretation: Most ASML contracts require customers to pay a down payment on systems to be shipped.
evidence_found: "In addition, most of our contracts require our customers to pay a down payment on systems to be shipped. We do not record a significant financing component for down payments" (20-F FY2025, Revenue note)
notes: Same note says 'other' refund liabilities rose in 2025 'mainly due to an increase of down payments refunded to customers'.

original_interpretation: Most ASML sales come from volume purchase agreements covering up to five years, with multiple performance obligations, negotiated discounts, and sometimes free goods, services or credits toward future purchases.
evidence_found: "The main portion of our net sales is derived from volume purchase agreements with our customers that have multiple performance obligations" ... "we may also offer free goods or services and credits that can be used toward future purchases." ... "volume purchase agreements with our customers which cover up to five years" (20-F FY2025, Revenue note)
notes: 'Up to five years' comes from the Remaining performance obligations paragraph.

original_interpretation: Teradyne recognises test-system hardware at a point in time and extended warranties, training, service agreements and software support over time.
evidence_found: "Teradyne’s hardware is typically recognized at a point in time upon transfer of control to the customer." ... "Extended warranty, training and support, service agreements and PCS are recognized over time based on the period of service." (10-K FY2025, Accounting Policies R15)
notes: Replacement parts are point-in-time.

original_interpretation: US$426 million (about 13%) of Teradyne's US$3,190 million 2025 revenue was recognised over time; the rest was point-in-time, mainly hardware.
evidence_found: Note E disaggregation, $ thousands, year ended Dec 31 2025: "Point in Time ... $ 2,763,951"; "Over Time ... 426,073"; "Total ... $ 3,190,024" (10-K FY2025, R18)
notes: Checker computed 426,073/3,190,024 = 13.4%. Point-in-time also includes replacement parts, so 'mainly hardware' is a reasonable reading, not a stated figure. Semi-test-only over-time (SoC+Memory+IST) = 342,128 thousand, matching the researcher note.

original_interpretation: PDF Solutions splits revenue into 'Platform' (software licences, SaaS, engineering services, characterisation fixed fees, DirectScan systems) and 'Volume-based' (Cimetrix runtime licences, secureWISE data, Gainshare).
evidence_found: "Platform revenue is derived from the following primary offerings: licenses for software (other than Cimetrix runtime licenses) ...; SaaS; engineering services; fixed fees associated with CV systems; and licenses and purchase contracts for DirectScan systems." "Volume-based revenue is derived from Cimetrix runtime licenses, secureWISE data, and Gainshare." (10-K FY2025, Note 2)
notes: Source says 'fixed fees associated with CV systems' (Characterization Vehicle); the claim paraphrases as characterisation fixed fees.

original_interpretation: PDF Solutions earns 'Gainshare' revenue tied to its customers' wafer manufacturing volumes, recognised in the period of usage and accrued from estimates before customer reports arrive.
evidence_found: "Revenue from Gainshare is typically recognized at a point in time based on customers’ wafer manufacturing volumes." ... "The Company typically recognizes Gainshare revenue in the same period in which the usage occurs. Because the Company generally does not receive the acknowledgment reports ... the Company accrues the related revenue based on estimates" (10-K FY2025, Note 2)

original_interpretation: 94% of PDF Solutions' 2025 revenue (US$219.0 million total) was classified as recurring and 6% as upfront.
evidence_found: "Recurring revenue (1) | 94 % | 81 % | 87 %"; "Upfront revenue (2) | 6 % | 19 % | 13 %" (2025/2024/2023); "Total revenue | $ 219,024" thousand (10-K FY2025, Note 2)
notes: Company-defined: recurring includes revenue that 'generally has often re-occurred in the past' (Cimetrix runtime licences, secureWISE data, Gainshare).

original_interpretation: PDF Solutions recognises SaaS as a subscription ratably over the subscription period, and perpetual licences at inception.
evidence_found: "Perpetual (one-time charge) license software is recognized at the time of the inception of the arrangement when control transfers" ... "is accounted for as a subscription and is recognized as revenue ratably, on a straight-line basis, over the subscription period" (10-K FY2025, Note 2)

original_interpretation: Entegris (fab materials and consumables) recognises substantially all revenue at a point in time on shipment or delivery; services are billed on time and materials.
evidence_found: "The Company recognizes revenue for product sales at a point in time ... which generally occurs upon shipment or delivery" ... "All material revenue is being recognized at a point in time." ... "The payment terms and revenue recognized are based on time and materials." (10-K FY2025, Note 1, R11)

original_interpretation: Entegris also licenses specialised manufacturing-process IP to customers for a royalty, recognised when the customer's sale or usage occurs.
evidence_found: "These arrangements typically permit the customer to use a specialized manufacturing process and in return the Company receives a royalty fee. The Company recognizes revenue for a sales-based or usage-based royalty promised in exchange for a license of intellectual property when the subsequent sale or usage occurs." (10-K FY2025, Note 1, R11)

original_interpretation: Of Entegris' US$3,196.6 million 2025 net sales, US$1,973.0 million came from fabs, US$469.4 million from equipment and engineering customers, US$320.1 million from chemical and materials companies and US$272.5 million from semiconductor distributors/other.
evidence_found: "(In millions) 2025 ... Semiconductor: Fabs$ 1,973.0 ... Equipment and Engineering 469.4 ... Chemical and Materials 320.1 ... Semi Distributor/Other 272.5 ... Non-Semi 161.6 ... Total net sales$ 3,196.6" (10-K FY2025, Note 2 Revenues, R12)
notes: The four listed categories are the semiconductor customers; the remaining US$161.6m is non-semi. 2024 fabs were 1,965.6.

original_interpretation: Linde's on-site (tonnage) gas supply contracts, used for the largest-volume customers, are total-requirement contracts of typically 10-20 years with minimum purchase requirements and price escalation, priced on formulas that move with price indices.
evidence_found: "Customers that require the largest volumes of product and that have a relatively constant demand pattern are supplied by cryogenic and process gas on-site plants." ... "On-site product supply contracts generally are total requirement contracts with terms typically ranging from 10-20 years and contain minimum purchase requirements and price escalation provisions." ... "pricing which fluctuates with various price indices." (10-K FY2025, Note 3, R28)
notes: Linde-wide policy, not electronics-specific (as researcher noted).

original_interpretation: Linde's merchant (bulk liquid) supply agreements usually run three to seven years without minimum purchase or volume commitments, and packaged-gas contracts one to three years.
evidence_found: "The customer agreements used in the merchant business are usually three to seven year supply agreements ... These contracts generally do not contain minimum purchase requirements or volume commitments." "Packaged gases are generally sold under one to three-year supply contracts and purchase orders and do not contain minimum purchase requirements or volume commitments." (10-K FY2025, Note 3)

original_interpretation: Linde lists electronic gases and specialty gases among its process gases and electronics among the industries it serves.
evidence_found: "process gases (hydrogen, helium, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, electronic gases, specialty gases, acetylene)" ... "Linde serves a diverse group of industries including healthcare, chemicals and energy, manufacturing, metals and mining, food and beverage, and electronics." (10-K FY2025, Note 3)

original_interpretation: AXT (compound-semiconductor substrates and refined gallium) sells mostly on short purchase orders (usually under six months) at prices set by a negotiated formula, list or fixed price, recognised on shipment, receipt or removal from consignment.
evidence_found: "Our products are typically sold pursuant to purchase orders" ... "The majority of our contracts have a single performance obligation to transfer products and are short term in nature, usually less than six months." ... "generally based upon a negotiated formula, list or fixed price." ... "upon shipment from our dock, receipt at the customer’s dock, or removal from consignment inventory" (10-K FY2025, Note 1, R14)

original_interpretation: AXT's 2025 revenue was 67% substrates and 33% raw materials (incl. purified gallium sold on the open market), produced through Chinese subsidiaries and joint ventures.
evidence_found: "In 2025, our substrate product group generated 67% of our revenue and raw materials product group generated 33%." ... "We use purified gallium in producing our GaAs substrates and also sell purified gallium in the open market" ... "Our consolidated subsidiaries produce and sell certain raw materials" (10-K FY2025, Note 1, R14)
correction: Revenue split verified. The page lists Chinese consolidated subsidiaries and JVs (Beijing Tongmei, Baoding Tongmei, ChaoYang units, JinMei) and says those subsidiaries produce raw materials. It does not state on this page where substrates are produced, so 'produced through Chinese subsidiaries and joint ventures' is only supported for raw materials.

original_interpretation: Siltronic (silicon wafers) reported that its 2025 wafer area sold rose while sales fell 4.7%, citing the weaker US dollar, 'price effects outside existing long-term agreements' and high customer inventories.
evidence_found: "In 2025, Siltronic AG generated sales of EUR 1,346.7 million, which was 4.7 percent below the previous year’s level" ... "The wafer area sold ... was above the previous year’s level. The depreciation of the US dollar ..., price effects outside existing long‑term agreements, and continued elevated inventories ... had a negative impact. The shutdown of the SD line during 2025 also accounted for roughly one third of the negative sales deviation"
correction: The claim leaves out two drivers Siltronic names: product mix effects, and the SD line shutdown, which Siltronic says caused roughly one third of the sales decline. Adjusted for FX and the SD shutdown, sales were flat year on year.
notes: Correctly typed reported_claim. EQS is the official wire for the company's own release, so company_documentation is acceptable.

original_interpretation: Siltronic's cash flow statement shows a EUR 25.9 million cash-effective change in customer prepayments in 2025 (EUR 26.0 million in 2024), so wafer customers prepay as well as fab customers of foundries.
evidence_found: Cash flow table "In EUR million 2025 2024 Change" ... "Cash-effective change in customer prepayments 25.9 26.0 –0.1" (Siltronic press release, 12 Mar 2026, section "Negative free and net cash flow due to high capital expenditure")
notes: Metric methodology says 'Audited financial statements (company filing)', but the source is a results press release; it should say 'company results press release'. The figure is a net cash inflow from prepayments, not the prepayment balance.

original_interpretation: Avnet recognises component sales at a point in time, generally on shipment, or later when goods consigned at customer locations are consumed; it drop-ships from suppliers in some cases.
evidence_found: "transfer of control to the customer generally occurs upon product shipment, but it may occur at a later date ... (such as delivery at the customer's designated location, or when products that are consigned at customer locations are consumed). In limited instances, where products are not in stock and delivery times are critical, product is purchased from the supplier and drop-shipped" (10-K FY2026, Note 1)
notes: Drop-shipping is 'in limited instances'.

original_interpretation: Avnet books revenue net, as an agent fee, where it only arranges products or services from another party, mainly supply-chain services and some supplier software.
evidence_found: "as the Company assumes an agency relationship in the transaction, revenue is recognized in the amount of the net fee associated with serving as an agent. These arrangements primarily relate to the sale of electronic component supply chain services or to a lesser extent supplier software services." (10-K FY2026, Note 1)

original_interpretation: Avnet records supplier consideration for price protection, rebates, sell-through incentives and marketing as reductions of product cost or SG&A, not as revenue.
evidence_found: "Vendor allowances and consideration —Consideration received from suppliers for price protection, product rebates, sell through incentives, marketing/promotional activities, or any other programs are recorded when earned ... as adjustments to product costs or selling, general and administrative expenses" (10-K FY2026, Note 1)

original_interpretation: Arrow is principal (gross revenue) when it negotiates pricing, pays the supplier, sets customer terms, handles returns and bears credit risk, and agent (net revenue) where it does not control the product.
evidence_found: "The company is the principal in transactions when it is principally responsible for fulfilling the order, which includes negotiating pricing, payment to the supplier, establishing payment terms with the customer, product returns, and has risk of loss if the customer does not make payment." ... "The company is the agent in these arrangements, which pertain to the sale of supplier-provided service contracts ... or delivery of product for which the company does not have control" (10-K FY2025, Note 1)
notes: Arrow is also principal for logistics/warehousing/financial services it provides itself.

original_interpretation: Arrow participates in supplier programs for price protection, product rebates and marketing allowances, booked as adjustments to cost of sales or SG&A.
evidence_found: "The company participates in supplier programs that provide for price protection, product rebates, marketing/promotional allowances, and other incentives. The consideration received under these programs is recorded ... as an adjustment to “Cost of sales” or “Selling, general, and administrative”" (10-K FY2025, Note 1, Vendor Programs)

original_interpretation: Alchip (ASIC design-service house) said NRE was between 30% and 40% of its Q3 2025 sales (US$223 million revenue), lifting gross margin to 28% from 21% in Q2 2025 as design milestones flowed in.
evidence_found: "Third quarter 2025 revenue declined to $223 million" ... "the third quarter 2025 gross margin improved to 28% from a second quarter 2025 gross margin of 21% as NRE contributed a higher percentage of sales, between 30% and 40% of sales. Third quarter 2025 NRE trended upward due to a strong inflow of design milestones." (Alchip Q3 2025 release, 2 Dec 2025; read via browser)
notes: Correctly a reported_claim (CEO statement). The 35 metric value is the midpoint of a range, as the methodology says.

original_interpretation: Alchip said NRE was less than 20% of its record Q1 2023 revenue when AI-chip production shipments dominated.
evidence_found: "Alchip Technologies has reported record revenue of USD$188 million for the first quarter of its 2023 fiscal year" ... "Historically strong artificial intelligent chip shipments to North American customer accounted for much of the significant jump in first quarter revenue ... NRE revenue accounted for less than 20 percent of first quarter FY2023 total revenue." (Alchip release, 23 May 2023; read via browser)
correction: The NRE share (<20%) and the record quarter (US$188m) are verified. Alchip says AI-chip shipments 'accounted for much of the significant jump' in revenue, not that they 'dominated' revenue.
notes: Historical data point (1Q23), not superseded.
